newsitem.title: CHINA: Shenzhen B shares inch down at noon in dull trade.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B shares inch down at noon in dull trade.

text.p: Shenzhen's hard currency B share index fell slightly in thin trading during the Monday morning session, with investors becoming more cautious as the interim corporate reporting season progresses, brokers said.
The index shed 0.01 points or 0.01 percent to 133.15 points on flimsy turnover of HK$10.4 million.
"People are reluctant to trade before any B share company releases its interim results," an analyst with a major Chinese brokerage said.
Listed companies must make public their 1997 interim earnings by August 30 but none of the 49 Shenzhen-listed B share companies has yet to do so.
Brokers said they expected sluggish trading would continue in coming sessions amid an absence of market-moving news.
The A share index gained 3.10 points or 0.74 percent to 422.73 points due in part to demand for shares of firms expected to post solid earnings, brokers said.
Turnover in the A share market was a modest 3.2 billion yuan.
Brokers said more investors were sidelined on Monday awaiting the results of a shareholders' meeting to be held by market leader Shenzhen Development Bank Ltd.
The bank, which was punished by Beijing for using bank funds to trade its own shares, was scheduled to hold the meeting on Tuesday to discuss its dividend plan based on 1996 profits.

Investors were afraid the bank might revise the plan -- which consisted of a five-for-10 bonus issue and a cash payout of 0.2 yuan per share -- after the seizure by authorities of illicit profits from the bank's own share trading of more than 90 million yuan, brokers said.
"Most investors will be watching the meeting tommorow," an analyst at Shenzhen J&A Securities said.
In the B share market, Shenzhen SEZ Real Estate was the worst performer, sinking HK$0.14 or 5.11 percent to HK$2.60 on thin volume of 2,000 shares.
In the A share market, Shenzhen Development Bank rose 0.27 yuan to 37.48 yuan on volume of 7.32 million shares, making it the most actively traded stock.
